title: Rent eviction by-law and school safety measures
subtitle: Also covered: a 20-storey-plus King Street West rezoning and new traffic rules near three new schools.
overview: The committee spent most of the evening on evictions due to renovations. After hearing from dozens of delegates, it recommended that staff look at a municipal by-law (Path 3) rather than only the lighter measures staff had proposed. Staff are to report to the June 23 Council meeting on timelines, costs and staffing for a by-law. The committee also recommended pursuing federal and provincial funding for affordable rental housing and continued advocacy for Ontario to enact its bad-faith eviction rules {{vote:m3}}.

The committee also recommended approving a rezoning for 924-944 King Street West, near Grand River Hospital, to allow a tall apartment building. Existing tenants would be covered by the City's Rental Replacement By-law {{vote:m2}}.
For school safety, the committee recommended lower speed limits, no-stopping zones, a bus loading zone and new crossing guards around schools opening in September 2025 {{vote:m1}}.
These are recommendations. Council will make the final decisions, starting with the Path 3 report on June 23.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing staff to report back on a possible renovation-eviction by-law (Path 3), including timelines, financial impacts and staffing, with funding applications and provincial advocacy.
The committee recommended approving the zoning by-law amendment and adopting the Urban Design Brief for the site.
The committee recommended 30 km/h and 40 km/h speed limits, no-stopping zones, a school bus loading zone and new crossing guards near three new elementary schools.

debate: Delegates opposing the staff approach said education and forums would not protect tenants, and that long Landlord and Tenant Board waits leave tenants exposed. They pointed to by-laws in other Ontario cities and argued that Bill 97 has not been enacted two years after passing.

Delegates described the stress of repeated eviction notices, particularly for seniors and long-term tenants, and argued the loss of affordable units adds to homelessness. One small landlord supported a by-law.

Staff said a by-law cannot stop a lawful eviction, only applies to certain notices, and has little track record elsewhere. They said it would need at least three new staff positions plus communications and other supports, and would displace existing housing work.

Some councillors worried a by-law would give false hope, duplicates provincial responsibility and needs more data first. Others said some hope and a deterrent were better than doing nothing and wanted to try Path 3 with a lean staffing option.
Several councillors defended staff against suggestions of bias.
